utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. Mr. Weber. Oh, you are just -- you're just ready to start.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kecman. I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Lukic, you have concluded your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Weber, if you're ready to cross-examine the witness, you may proceed. And you'll be cross-examined, Mr. Kecman, by Mr. Weber. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kecman.

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, today I'd first like to start by clarifying each of your assignment between the year of 1991 to 1993. You were assigned to a squadron based at the Zeljava airport between 28 June 1991 and 20 October 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a squadron commander. I was just a -- the commander of one part of that squadron.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, please listen to my questions carefully. They'll be -- I'll try to keep them very clear. Do I understand correctly, then, you were assigned to the Zeljava airport between 28 June and 20 October 1991?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Zeljava airport was on the border between the Republic of Croatia and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is -- just so we have a little context, it's the south of Slunj and to the north of Korenica; right?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's east of Korenica and south of Slunj. So you're right. It would be north-west of the town of Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. In paragraph 21 of your statement you indicate that you were assigned to a helicopter regiment in Zaluzani near Banja Luka on 20 October 1991. Were you a part of this regiment from 20 October until the beginning of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were assigned to the 711th Anti-Armour Helicopter Squadron or POHE of the 5th Corps prior to April 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 5th Corps and there was indeed a 711th squadron and I was its member.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32545 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 1 April 1992 order number 1-763 from Lieutenant-General Bozidar Stevanovic, commander of the air force and anti-aircraft defence. At the beginning of this order, we see that it relates to the temporary assignment of personnel to a helicopter squadron of the Ministry of Interior of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the B/C/S and page 3 of the English translation. Focusing on item number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under item 5, we see that you are listed and your previous assignment is described. The order then indicates that you received a temporary assignment as of 1 April. You were assigned to a helicopter squadron of the MUP of the SAO Krajina as of 1 April 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this document, we see there is an instruction to report to the commander of the Udbina airport. If could you just give us the name, who did you report to when you received this assignment?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The squadron was set up in the Republic of Serbian Krajina. It was directly subordinated to the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you give us the name of the person who you reported to when you received this assignment?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My superior was Major Darko Sekulic. He was the commander of that squadron.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And the squadron that you're referring to, I believe we see, according to report, is the 56th Mixed Helicopter Squadron.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you also please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you in this helicopter squadron until November 1993?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As a member of this squadron, you are familiar with the 17th of August training centre in Golubic; right?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name doesn't ring a bell. What do you mean when you say the training centre? Could you be more specific, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: First of all, could the Prosecution tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7372, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7372 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And since you just asked that last question, if we could go quickly to 65 ter 32547, page 2 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before that. Mr. Registrar, 65 ter 25760b, what P number does it have? I have it as having 7372.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. So 65 ter number 32545 will be P7373.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Sorry, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a 31 May 1994 RSK MUP 56th Helicopter Squadron request. It's addressed to the RSK minister of internal affairs. In the first line of the request, it refers to your former unit being based at the Golubic training centre, and in the third sentence the request indicates that the helicopter squadron moved to the Heliodrom on 28 September 1993. Does this help you refresh your recollection as to the 17th of August training centre in Golubic?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the place Golubic, and I'm familiar with the signature of the commander, Lieutenant-Colonel Veljko Leka. That's all I know about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I wasn't going to spend much time on this, but since I had to use this on the record, it's part of a larger file, if Your Honours would, with your indulgence, if we could just excerpt the one document and tender that one document. We're not going to need to seek the entire file at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you think that that's enough, I leave it in your hands, Mr. Weber, but you then have to separately upload it as a separate document. We could already reserve a number for this extract of what was until now uploaded under the number you mentioned. But this is the 31st of May 1994 request for hangar construction. Mr. Registrar, the number to be reserved would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would be P7373, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 7374, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, P7374 is reserved for that purpose. Witness, you said you didn't know anything more about this document. Now, the document refers to the 17th of August training centre. Do you say that is totally unknown or I'm not aware of any Golubic training centre? Apart from whether you have seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've not seen this document before. I'm familiar with the centre at Golubic. One part of my unit was there in January 1993, when the units of the Croatian army attacked the southern part of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are familiar with the centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would have saved some time if you would have told us that right away when you were asked about the 17th August training centre Golubic, rather than to invite Mr. Weber to describe what training centre he meant. Because, as it turns out now, you're fully aware of that training centre. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32546 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 5 February 1992 order from RSK Minister of the Interior Milan Martic. At the bottom of the document, we see there's a reference to the previous order that we look the at a little bit ago. Number 1-763. We also see that you are referred to under item 1 and it indicates that you are the mixed air squadron commander. You've mentioned that you became the commander of this squadron during your testimony. My question to you is: When did you become the commander?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I became acting commander on the 16 November 1994 after my squadron commander was killed. I was temporarily assigned to his position until the official order which came on the 5th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm a little bit confused by the date that's recorded in the transcript. Sir, if you could clarify. Your previous answer says -- starts with you saying: "I became acting commander on 16 February [sic] 1994..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: November.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: 16 November, sorry, of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is that an accurate date?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see here and as far as I can remember, it was in 1993. I apologise. 1992. And then in 1993 I became the squadron commander starting with this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on what we've seen, is it correct that you were assigned to the RSK MUP Ministry of Interior between 1 April 1992 and November 1993?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to that unit, I stayed there until the 1st of April, 1993. And after that date, another unit was set up and it was part of the armed forces of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. I continued working as commander in that unit and that unit remained part of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now I just want to ask you about a couple aspects of the document before us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, I understood your question that you'd like to know when he was appointed, not until when he stayed. Which seems to be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I actually changed from when he was appointed commander, which I believe he clarified. I then -- it was my intention to move on to the fact of whether or not he was assigned to the MUP --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I may have -- is it correct that you were assigned to the RSK MUP ministry between the 1st of April 1992 and November 1993. I would expect an answer when he was assigned and he told us until when he stayed, but where he exactly stayed is even not clear. But if you are satisfied with the answer, then I leave it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to direct your attention to the fact that Milan Martic sends this order to the VJ General Staff personnel administration, we can see that at the top of the document. This was because you were assigned to the RSK MUP through the 40th Personnel Centre of the VJ; right?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what personnel centre and what administration it was. I was assigned this way and this is all okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just to understand correctly, you were assigned to the RSK MUP through the VJ; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you later joined the Army of Republika Srpska, you were also assigned to the VRS through the VJ; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was assigned at my own request, which I sent to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. My request was to move to Republika Srpska, this was accepted, and I rejoined the Army of Republika Srpska as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That request went through Belgrade; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, before tendering this document, I just wanted to draw your attention to the reference to Federal Secretary of National Defence order number 1943-1 of 28 April 1992 in the first part of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I tender this document at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 32546 will be Exhibit P7375, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7375 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 14426 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, sir, coming up before you will be order number 1943-1, dated 28 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe it starts on the next page as the enclosure in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, did I miss the translation of the handwritten portions on the cover page. Could we go one page back? In both versions. I see quite some handwriting which appears not to be translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. We -- we see that that's the case. When I go to tender, I'd be happy to address that -- or what I'm focusing on for the examination is the actual order itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's move on. But, of course, the Chamber would like to know what is written there. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for drawing our attention to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we move on to the second page in both versions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is order number 1943-1, dated 28 April, 1992, from Blagoje Adzic, chief of the General Staff of the SFRY armed forces. We can see that the order relates to organisational changes in the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Could the Prosecution please go to the next page of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under item 7 of this order, we see that there's a reference to the 56th Combined Air Force Squadron at the Udbina airport. This is referring to your helicopter squadron; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The order then indicates that in peacetime and in war time the squadron shall be resubordinated to the RSK Ministry of Interior. We have seen from the previous documents that you were formally assigned to the RSK MUP, and here we see that your squadron it resubordinated to the MOD. During operations you were resubordinated to the military; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was resubordinated to the Ministry of Interior. However, this is about a different system. Up until the 1st of May, 1995, the activities which took place in the Republic of Serbian Krajina were supervised by the peacekeeping forces and the authority fell into the hands of the Ministry of Interior. It was only after that that the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina was re-established.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, the Chamber has received some other evidence about this. I'm not going to spend a lot of time with you on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So could the Prosecution please tender this document. We'd be happy to have it marked for identification pending the revision -- the revised translation of the cover page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI P7376, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to clean up -- Your Honours, to clean up a housekeeping matter. The excerpted page from 65 ter 32547, the 31 May 1994 document, has now been uploaded into e-court under 65 ter 32547a. This document was provisionally assigned Exhibit P7375. We now ask that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: 7374. Thank you, Your Honours. We kindly request that the document be replaced and it now be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. P7374 is admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play a video, and it is 65 ter 22312a. I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to pause at the 14-second mark at the outside of the video. We have provided transcripts to the booths, and there's minimal audio on the video so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Minimal is not nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Not nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you rely in any way on the audio?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The audio that is there, at this first portion there's -- there's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has it been verified that the transcript reflects the words spoken? Because if not, we have to play it twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No it hasn't been verified, although this video has been admitted in multiple times as exhibits at the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This video in this trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Not in this trial. But at the trial -- previous occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: But it has not been verified in this record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Chamber has a standard procedure for verifying whether especially quickly spoken text is accurately reflected in the transcript and then interpreted for us accurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, we do it twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The video is now paused at 14.1 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, what you have just seen the beginning of is footage from a March 1992 video recording that took place at the 17th of August training centre in Golubic. Do you recognise the person saluting here towards the right side of the photo as Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in the first 14 seconds of this video we saw Mr. Martic walking in front of a number of individuals in uniform. These people in uniform that we've seen so far, they were members of the RSK MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is footage from the training centre that we spoke of a moment ago, the 17th of August. And as far as I can see, this is one of these groups of soldiers -- or rather policemen who were in that centre and who were completing their training at that centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just so we have it on the record before we continue watching, did you attend this ceremony or know about it in March 1992?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know. You saw from that order that I arrived in the unit, that is to say, the Republika Srpska Krajina, on the 1st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yeah. Could we please continue watching until 2 minutes and 25 seconds. There will be a song, I believe, played during this portion, and then there will be some verbally spoken words, so it may require us to go back and reverify those words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll replay the portion where, as you said, words were spoken verbally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I noted that there was spoken portions between the approximately 33 second mark to 47 seconds, and 2 minutes 12 seconds to approximately the 2.25.2 mark that we're on. If Your Honours would like, we could replay those two segments right now, skipping -- [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then we'd like to hear the interpretation of those words.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: First, may I ask Ms. Stewart to replay from approximately 33 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Cadets, I salute you."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could continue playing until approximately 47 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Good afternoon, sir. Very good. Attention. Stand at ease."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if we could now please go to -- just to start a little early, the 2 minute, 10 second mark, and if we could continue playing until the 2 minutes 25 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Please allow me on behalf of the 17th August training centre here in the Republika of Serbian Krajina to welcome... "

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm just pausing here. Aside from Mr. Martic, and I believe you also recognised General Mladic in this video, did you recognise any other individuals who were present that we've seen so far?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for my two commanders, I recognise the president of Republic of Serb Krajina, Mr. Goran Hadzic. That would be it, roughly. It was pretty fast. That's what I managed to recognise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We're paused at 2 minutes, 25 seconds. Is it correct that President Hadzic is sitting in the dark overcoat with the beard in the image that's on the screen before us?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And when you're saying your two commanders, who are the individuals that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first my commander was Mr. Milan Martic, and afterwards my commander was General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I'm going to play the remainder of the video, and it's going to need to be played twice because there's words spoken throughout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's hear it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And at this time the Prosecution has got to replay from the 2 minute 25 second portion till the end of the video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Mr. Zdravko Zecevic, prime minister of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Interruption. Representatives of the Krajina Corps led by Major-General Ratko Mladic. The commander of the Serb Volunteer Guard. The president of ... "Dear guests of this [unintelligible] ceremony for all the soldiers who fell for our Krajina, may they rest in eternal glory, against the Ustasha, about the defence against the dagger, about the defence of the Serb people not only in the Krajina but throughout our blood soaked Serbian land, because you must know that this has never been Croatia, the Serb people paid for this land with blood, I say to you that this never belonged to Croatia. This is Serbia and will stay Serbia."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, toward the end of this video, we saw the statements by Zeljko Raznjatovic, who's known to this Chamber as Arkan, and we can also hear the applause when he says: "This is Serbia and will stay..." part of "... Serbia." This last statement by Zeljko Raznjatovic, this was a reference to the Republic of Serbian Krajina; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection. I don't know how this witness who was not there would know what Zeljko Raznjatovic meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then he'll tell us that he doesn't know and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that it would be pure guessing, Your Honours, and that's why we would object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at least the word "Krajina" is mentioned not only once but twice in the speech. So, therefore, the question can be asked to the witness and you may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Raznjatovic's reference "to this is Serbia and will stay..." a part of "... Serbia" is a reference to the Republic of Serbian Krajina; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the Serb people were in that area and they didn't want to leave the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and those processes, I mean international processes, had not been carried out, my personal view is that that is the context in which he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 22312a into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7377, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7377 is admitted. I see that the CD-ROMs have been provided. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I just have a couple of other really small items to discuss with you, and I'd actually like to direct your attention now forward while you were in the Army of Republika Srpska, so between 1993 and 1995. During that time, did you ever fly to the VMA in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32576 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, what's going to be coming up before you is going to be an aerial image from Google of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Can we see it on the monitor already?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No document attached to the 65 ter, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, our apologies. If could you have a moment of indulgence, I believe it's being released. Your Honours, I note I do not have it on the screen before me. I don't know if it's on the screen before the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not on our screens. It wasn't on our screens because it is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Here we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is an aerial image of Belgrade. The installations towards the centre of the aerial image, you recognise that as the VMA in Belgrade; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could direct our attention to the -- there's two circles with -- appear to be paved paths around them just below and a little to the right of the VMA, those are helicopter landing pads; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if we could just do as of -- if you could do us a favour just because there's lot of things on this photograph. If the court officer could please hand the witness with -- a pen, and if could you circle the helicopter landing pads.

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: These are the helicopter landing pads you landed at during the war; right?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you fly to the VMA in Belgrade ever from Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you fly to the -- to this location from anywhere in Eastern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not asking to you explain the occasions, but if could you just tell us the precise locations that you flew from in eastern -- from Eastern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Zvornik, the location of Karakaj where the Heliodrom was. I flew the wounded to Belgrade, to this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just so we have some idea of timing, from the Heliodrom in Karakaj to the VMA in Belgrade, approximately how long would that take you to fly between those two points?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 20 to 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the image on the screen, as marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As marked by the witness. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7378, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7378 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber. Any questions in re-examination, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very -- very short. Can I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day once again, Mr. Kecman.

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am just going ask you something about this video that was shown to you now, P7377. That's how it's been admitted. We saw this speech by Zeljko Raznjatovic. Do you know who filmed this material?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there. I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, does this footage show that this is exactly the gathering where Zeljko Raznjatovic is speaking?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see that he is speaking, but I cannot say specifically where it is that he is speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me just ask you something. Zeljko Raznjatovic has been mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just for my understanding, you have not specifically asked, is there a suggestion that the speech by Zeljko Raznjatovic is planted into that video and is not part of the ceremony?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The suggestion is that we do not see where Zeljko Raznjatovic spoke. There is no -- any connection in that video. It was just cut and we saw him [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but he's announced, isn't it, by the main speaker? Well, not by name but by function.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But we do not know if that speech is from that meeting. We cannot -- I couldn't see it. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say -- yes. You said there's no link and I'm just wondering whether you consider the announcement of a person in a certain position speaking -- is not then related to Arkan? Is that your position or do you say we don't know?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I could not establish that that speech was from that meeting. Although he was announced, it doesn't mean that that's -- that was a speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, of course. It could be anything else. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kecman, Zeljko Raznjatovic is speaking here in this video footage about the struggle against daggers. What are daggers and what are they a symbol are?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Daggers are a symbol of the Ustasha; that is to say, everything negative that happened to the Serb people during the previous war, that is to say, from 1941 to 1945.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was this that happened to the Serb people and what are daggers related to?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A major genocide was carried out against the Serb people. About a million and a half Serbs lost their lives during that war. You saw these daggers, that these daggers were used in the camp of Jasenovac, where 500- to 700.000 persons lost their lives. Not only Serbs but other ethnic groups as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Serb Republic of Krajina, do you know whether Zeljko Raznjatovic was subordinated to the Army of Yugoslavia, actually the JNA at the time?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I think he was not. I mean, I know he was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kecman. That's all we had for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, any further questions? But let me just -- any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would just like to go to a quick time-frame in that video, if we could. Exhibit P7377, time code 3 minute, 19 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in this video in the front row, do you see General Mladic standing towards the -- he's the individual in the front row, second to the left of the photo; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And we've seen Mr. Raznjatovic and what he was wearing that day, but is it correct that if you go over three individuals from General Mladic, towards President Hadzic, that's Zeljko Raznjatovic standing in the second row; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One last question. You started saying I'm not certain whether Arkan was subordinated, and then you said you think he was not, and then you say "I know he was not." Could you explain what was at the basis of this knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, knowing Mr. Mladic from the subsequent period, I mean, he certainly would not have paramilitaries within his own troops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say you concluded that in view of the attitude taken later by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic had that attitude from the very beginning until the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you said subsequent period. Why did you refer to the subsequent period?

utterances.speaker: JANKO KECMAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that situation; namely, that I participated and waged war in three different armies; that is to say, all the three armies that General Ratko Mladic belonged to. Knowing from the very outset when I heard of him in 1991, 1992, when I heard about his attitudes and his way of protecting the confronted parties in that area, he certainly had enough power and he didn't need any help from the outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions triggered by my questions? Mr. Kecman, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you; questions that were put to you by the parties, questions that were put to you by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honour. It would be Mr. Todorovic, Dragan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom -- oh, no, we'll first take a break. I have to apologise. We take a break and we resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Todorovic. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Todorovic. Mr. Todorovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You find Mr. Lukic to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, could you please tell us slowly your name, your first and last names.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Todorovic. I was born on the 8th of August, 1965 in Tuzla. Before the war, I resided in Kladanj municipality. My father's surname Mirosav, my mother's name is Nevenka. I'm a Serb of Orthodox faith and I'm a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Hvala [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Until when did you reside in Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Until the beginning of the war. Until 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now I'm going to ask you something about the situation before the war broke out. First of all, did you know anything about the military organisation of Muslims in 1991, from 1991 until the spring of 1992 in Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Since I lived and worked in Kladanj, obviously I knew what was going on in my municipality. I myself got an invitation from the TO Kladanj to report to a mobilisation spot. The name of that is Tisovac; it's a dam, a bathing spot. I never responded because I did not want to be a member of the Patriotic League. Nobody ever forced me to respond. I worked at a hotel as a waiter. From time to time, those people would go for maneuvers. I saw them in uniforms with white markings on their hats. It was the symbol of a lily and the letters PL for Patriotic League. It was not like all the population sported those symbols and insignia. Some people did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long or how late was it safe to travel and when did it become unsafe to use the roads around Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When barricades and check-points emerged, all that didn't bode well. That demonstrated that things had changed, that we were looking at each other differently, that we were behaving differently, that we were controlling each other, that the mutual trust that had existed all of a sudden was dying out. People started avoiding their former friends and acquaintances. Guards started patrolling the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you leave Kladanj, approximately? At what time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I left Kladanj at the end of April or the beginning of May. A man in uniform came. He was my neighbour. And he told me, "Go. I can help you today. I won't be able to help you tomorrow." I just laughed. I asked for an explanation. He said I can't explain. We had socialised. We had worked together. He told me go and join your people. I accepted that. I realised that it was not a joke. I went to my village, to where my parents lived. I stayed there for a while. And from there, I left. In my village, they thought it was just a game, that war. I told them that people had uniforms and arms, and they said it's all a big joke. I left there, I left my village across the forest, I arrived in Vlasenica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting but it was a simple question: When did you leave. And as he has with the other questions, he's getting into a repeated narrative. So I would ask for simple question/answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, I do not know whether this is what you're seeking, Mr. Lukic, in that the witness apparently feels what your next question would be. But I asked myself at all what is the part of it if there's any dispute. Is there any dispute that a Patriotic League did exist, Mr. McCloskey? There's no dispute about that. Is there any dispute that it happened -- that it existed in Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't believe so, Mr. President. But as for these details, I'm not absolutely clear on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then it's all sweeping statements without any basis of knowledge. Mr. Lukic, this Chamber would very much like to receive serious evidence challenging what the Prosecution seeks to establish. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was just an entry for my next several questions, and I think it would be clear from the next one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I would say move directly to what you consider to be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Todorovic, what do you personally know about what happened to the Serbs who had remained in Kladanj after you left?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The Serbs who stayed in Kladanj, some of them joined the military, and those who refused to join were taken to a camp. Some were arrested at the check-points and their trace was lost until the year 2000. I'm talking about four lads: Dragan Zelenovic, Dragan Remetic, Vojo Baletic, and Vojislav Vasiljevic. They're my relatives, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what did you learn about them and when did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We learned that after the war there was a long search for them, before that, on our part, and then we learned that they were killed not far from Kladanj in the direction of Vrtenovic in a cave. Their bodies were exhumed from there and those who were in the camp survived. And those who were in the camp survived thanks to the Red Cross organisations -- organisation that registered them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know anything about those four relatives of yours? Where were they killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We didn't know anything. They were arrested before a combat event started. At the check-point, the Patriotic League took them prisoner. A detachment had been set up. They arrested them. They were supposed to be investigated. And after that, all their traces were lost until the end of the war. During the war, we tried to get in touch with the military to see if we could find them, if we could exchange them. Nothing came out of that. We didn't know anything about their destiny until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In combat with the opposing side, did you lose a family member?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Two uncles and a relative. I was the 17th in a row that was wounded, but I survived. Those who were wounded before me didn't survive. They were wounded in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the area where you were, were there any civilian casualties on the Serbian side during combat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Around Kladanj, there were civilian casualties when our villages were being attacked. All the villages around the Kladanj municipality were torched save for Pelemis. They were torched in 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down and could he repeat the two names that he has just mentioned of his uncle and his relative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, first of all, could you slow down and could you repeat the two names you'd just mentioned of your uncle and a relative.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My uncle on my father's side, not my uncle on my mother's side, Nikola Todorovic; and my relative, Nebojsa Zoranovic. They were both killed while they were defending my village, Vucinici, not far from Kladanj. My uncle was taken prisoner after he had been wounded, and then he was finished off and killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when was that? Because we have no time-frame whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1992. I believe that it was in the month of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked you about civilian casualties.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were in other villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the names of those villages where there were civilian casualties but slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Vrenovici, Mladovo, Obrcevac, Pajici, Kovacici, Konjevic Vucinici and other villages whose names escape me. All the villages were destroyed. The houses were torched there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Pelemis as an exception to that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the village of Pelemis remain intact until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What happened and when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Pelemis was attacked on Easter Day in 1993. Strong Muslim forces attacked the village. That was the Army of BiH. I don't know what you want me to call that force. I don't want to insult anybody. I'm going to use the term "BiH army."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, two questions: First, you said you mentioned Pelemis as an exception to that. I don't find that on the record, so it may have been that the -- if I'm not mistaken. And second, if the witness describes what happened in many, many villages, it would certainly assist us if we would know what his personal knowledge about all that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, you heard what Judge Orie's interested in. What is your personal knowledge about the torched Serb villages in Kladanj municipality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: My personal knowledge is this: In Obrcevac, Mladovo, and Vrenovici, there were civilian casualties of advanced age: My uncle, whose name I mentioned, and my relative, whose names I mentioned, were killed in my village, and I also know that all the houses were torched. They burnt to the ground. They were completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you present when it happened or did you learn about your uncle later or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I learned about my uncle's death in the year 2000 when his body was found and exhumed. Until then he been recorded as a missing person. And for as long as a person is recorded as missing, there is a search for their body. That's normal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now the circumstances under which your uncle died, did you learn that from others who have observed that or did you not learn it? Is it still unknown to you? I'd like to know what -- how you learned these things. I do understand that if a body is exhumed, then that's a way of learning that somebody had died, and not very pleasant, I fully understand that, but do you have any other direct information about, for example, what happened to your uncle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My uncle was a member of the Army of Republika Srpska that had also been set up at the same time as the BiH army. He defended his own village. There was an attack on my village in August. He was wounded in his left leg when they took him prisoner. He was taken prisoner, and as soon as that happened he was finished off. He was killed. And for Nebojsa Zoranovic, his body remained hidden until the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now my question is: Who told you that he was killed and when, and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who told me? A mate of mine who was in Italy who had worked with me. He returned, opened a restaurant. Since we were good friends before the war, I got in touch with him and he told me that he would find the grave and mark it but that he didn't dare be present for his own personal safety reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question. Who took your uncle prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The BiH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where did they take him prisoner from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the direction of Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On what date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember the date. I know that it was in August 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you witness the taking of him as a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did this friend who opened a restaurant, did he tell you where he was when your uncle was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He wanted to avoid the war and then he returned to Bosnia after the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So he was not present when your uncle was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what then exactly is the basis of his knowledge? How did he know further details, if he did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. He had own men there. That was his town. He knew the lads who had been engaged. He got in touch with somebody I don't know. In any case, he helped me to excavate the bodies. A doctor from Zvornik called Gavro [phoen] went with the Red Cross, they excavated the body, they marked the area where the bodies had been buried.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you about any names. I'm just going to ask you the ethnicity of that mate of yours who helped you to locate your uncle's body?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Muslim, Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After leaving Kladanj, where did the Serb refugees go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Some in Vlasenica, some in Zvornik, some in Sekovici, some in Serbia. Some stayed on the lines as personnel, the newly established line of combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who had military obligation on Serb territory? Did Muslims also have to go into the army as well as Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When I joined the Army of Republika Srpska, it was voluntary, and in my unit there wasn't a single Muslim in that first unit where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, were Muslims forcibly recruited into the Serb army in your territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In my territory, Vlasenica-Sekovici, I'm not aware of anybody receiving call-up papers and being forcibly brought into the unit as a combatant or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you briefly about your participation in the army. You said that you joined voluntarily. What unit, when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived Vlasenica, I reported to the municipality in Vlasenica and they deployed me in Sekovici, the Sekovici Brigade, and that's why I joined the ranks of the Sekovici Brigade. I think it was the 1st Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where did you go after that unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, an assault detachment was detached in Vlasenica, I think it was September, so I joined that assault detachment of Vlasenica that was subordinated to the Drina Corps that was already established by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that unit, did you stay in the VRS all the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I spent some time in that unit. And then from that unit, I went to the special unit of the police, the Sekovici 2 Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, not very long. Didn't really like it there. I didn't like the behaviour of the command towards us. And also I'm not a fan of blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I went back to this Vlasenica Intervention Platoon that was attached to the command. I was there until I was wounded on the Vlasenica-Kladanj road.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After recovering from that wound --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness start again. We didn't hear the beginning of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, could you restart your answer, because the interpreters missed the beginning of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I was wounded on the road between Vlasenica and Kladanj during the night on the 27th of July, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you recover during the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After recovery, did you go back or did you go to some other unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: After recovery, I joined the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the number of the military post code that he referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- could you, could you please repeat the number of the military post code that you mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 75. 7572/15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where was this unit based? Was it in one place only?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. Some were in Bijeljina and some had their base in Vlasenica. A smaller place, a village, about 5 kilometres away. The name is Dragasevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What part were you in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I was in the Vlasenica part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the purpose of that unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's a unit that was established to work behind enemy lines, to destroy enemy manpower, soldiers, materiel. To carry out sabotage behind enemy lines. Also certain things like securing officers, important buildings, and so on, when necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was your commander in that unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Commander Milorad Pelemis was my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 1994 and 1995, do you know which rank Mr. Pelemis held?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, he never wore any kind of insignia, and he didn't like us to address him that way. I think it was second lieutenant, lieutenant, something like that. I think that that is what he managed to attain even by the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What were your duties within the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, since I had been wounded, I have these scars from the war, five bullets. He offered me to work on logistics, to take care of soldiers so that they could eat on time, so that they could have a place to sleep, that they would have clothes to wear, footwear, and it seemed to me that I could handle that. I accepted that. I did that from one task to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you go out into the field with the unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were out in the field, did your role change or were you still in charge of the same things like in base?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, basically I did all the same things while we were in the field. If the unit moved, I moved together with them. If the unit was in jeopardy, of course, I would help my pals and the soldiers, officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you would go into action, did you get any instructions from Commander Pelemis before each and every action; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What were you told before these actions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, every time he would line up the unit and present what he had to say, how we were supposed to behave in this action, what we were supposed to do, that we were supposed to help one another, that we were supposed to save one another, and even if the worst were to happen, then how we should eliminate one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In which cases was a member of the unit supposed to be eliminated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: If the rest of the team was under threat, the rest of the group, the platoon, depending on the number of personnel involved and what was being done. So if any of these people were a threat to other soldiers, making them a target for falling into some kind of danger, getting arrested or captured or killed, then the commander of the group would decide to have him eliminated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In practice, did it ever happen that a member of the group was liquidated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. And thank God for that, that did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you told how to treat civilians that you find on enemy territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: All civilians that were encountered, they were supposed to be greeted or people were supposed to go around them, and I don't know of a single civilian being touched in any way, when people went into action. They tried to pacify them and, if possible, even to avoid them. It was the enemy that was the target. Their heavy weaponry, their lines, their vehicles. That's what saboteurs do: You attack the enemy so that the enemy would not attack you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us mentally move to the month of July 1995. Do you remember whether your unit was given a task in relation to Srebrenica in the beginning of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see on our screens D320. We saw this document several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I have no recollection what D320 is. But if it is any document you are seeking confirmation of, then the -- in-chief, the appropriate way of doing that is to first ask a question. And then if you think that the answer requires that you put a document to the witness that you do it then. Not to show it to him and then -- because that may have a leading effect. But, again, I do not know what your question will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask this witness about the signature on this document, so I had to have it front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you have to do it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Todorovic, there is a document before you. At the bottom of this document it says: "Commander, 2nd Lieutenant Pelemis."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Pelemis, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Mr. Pelemis's signature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this his signature, the one that we see in the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this signature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is this, Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Franc Kos's. He was a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, a second lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In real time, when this document was issued, did you see it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my document, and I submitted this document to the Tribunal. I had this document, and I prepared personnel and equipment and everything else that was needed on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is an order for the unit to march along the Bijeljina-Vlasenica-Bratunac axis?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did people go towards Bratunac on the basis of this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the moment when the order was received to go to Bratunac, out of this group, who knew where the group was going? Did everybody know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Only I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who did you inform about this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When we linked, only Franc knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say Franc?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Franc Kos.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where did you go and did you go on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we went in the direction of Bratunac. Am I supposed to tell you which road we took?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it the road that is marked here in the order?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't understand the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So where did you arrive and where did you spend the night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, up there, near Zeleni Jadar, some trenches, some forest, some road ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next day, the 11th of July, 1995, what do you remember at first in the morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In the morning, there was this attack by the BH Army, and they managed to recapture territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After they managed to recapture some territory, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a counter-attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Counter-attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Of our army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you enter Srebrenica on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did you get going? How did you move to Srebrenica? Who did you receive orders from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: From our commander, Milorad Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you part of one of the groups that entered Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the group of Luka Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Number 16 in this document, that's Luka Jokic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I am right below him. He's a sergeant; I'm a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where did your group go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Since I hadn't been in Srebrenica before the war, I didn't really know the town. We started out from some plum orchard, that is where they got this command from Mr. Pelemis. He said that we were given the assignment to enter and that he was not satisfied with that but we had to go there because we were given that order. We did not know about urban warfare. He said that we should take care of one another, that we should not take any risks, that we should not touch anything if we're not sure that we can get through. If we come across some obstacle on the road, that is to say, mines and stuff like that, that we should not touch that, that some other unit would come, that we should try to go around that. If we encounter soldier, that we should try to get him to surrender. If he opens fire, that we should return fire. If civilians go out in front of us to make a barricade or something or if they show up from their houses, that we should avoid victims, casualties on either side at any cost. Also, he said that we should be careful when entering because there would be a change of clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who would be changing clothes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Soldiers of the BH Army. And that then they can be the same kind of danger like when they wear uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How far did you get?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Our objective was to reach the police station and we assumed that that's where the commander was of this gentleman who commanded their 28th Division. I don't know what his rank was. His name is Naser Oric and also that that we should blockade all important facilities, that we should search the area, that we should not allow anyone to touch documentation, that everything should be written down, registered, recorded, that it should all be put in one place so that it could be taken over by our army and our organs, the people who deal with this kind of paperwork, intelligence, counter-intelligence, so that they could see whether there were any traces of lists of prisoners, of torture, of arrests, of interrogations of our people, our personnel who were taken prisoner in the surrounding area around the protected area of Srebrenica. We did all of that and that was all on the orders -- the boss's order; that is to say, Pelemis's order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question, Witness, was how far did you get, and then you told us in many many lines all kind of things. But the simple question was how far did you get. Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have. It's in the first line. Line 3 of page 41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, that was the objective. Not the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what the objective was, Mr. Lukic, and an objective is not necessarily always what you achieve. So therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if you thought that you had received an answer in the first line, you should have stopped the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, how far did you reach with your group? I don't know whether you heard my question. Could you please tell us how far did you reach with your group on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We went slowly and surely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you reach the police station that was your objective?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, ultimately we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was, but I tried to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, you can't try. Where -- how far did you get. Insist on your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who was there with you? Did you move along the same road like everybody else who reached the same point, the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Some went along the left flank, some along the right, some were in the middle. We searched houses. It's not easy to enter a town that had been held by the BiH army until an hour ago. You could expect anything, an ambush, mines, explosives. You had to have eyes in the back of your head. You did not dare touch anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, nobody asked you where you needed eyes. The question was: Who was there with you. Could you tell us that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Luka Jokic was in my group, Vlastimir Golijan, Milos Martic, Aleksandar Djuric, Goran Lulic, Zoran Stupar. These are the names that come to mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there any resistance when you entered the town of Srebrenica itself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: There was no major resistance. When I say resistance, I mean an army countering another army. There were some shots, there were some people whistling, but I wouldn't call that resistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see any civilians in the town of Srebrenica itself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What were the civilians doing? Were they standing, moving, what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: At first they didn't know who we were and who -- whose army we were members of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was at first. Then after that, did they realise that you were the Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the end, they did. We told them that we had arrived in Srebrenica, that they should not be afraid, that we would not harm them. Nobody touched anybody. We moved them aside. We checked if somebody had a uniform. They were behind our backs and we just continued on our way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the civilians move behind you or did they stay behind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: They were some 100 metres behind us or even more. But at that moment, I could not measure any distances because I was too worried for my own life.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, did you spend the entire day in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then in the evening or the night between the 11th and the 12th where were you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We withdrew to the entrance of Srebrenica, in the direction of the Srebrenica-Zeleni Jadar road. We took up three houses there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you arrived close to the police station in that part of Srebrenica, did you see Milorad Pelemis there, your commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you know Drazan Erdemovic? Did you know him from before the 11th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see him had in that part of Srebrenica? In the centre of Srebrenica, that is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the morning on the 12th, what did you do? Let's focus on the 12th of July then. Do you remember what you did on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I got up, like every morning. I was with my troops. We had breakfast.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After breakfast, did you stay there, did you leave, how many of you stayed behind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelemis ordered me and the driver to get ready and to leave for Dragasovaci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We got the village -- didn't -- I don't think the interpreters quite got the correct village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you again give the name of that village. And please pronounce it slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dragasovac. Dragasovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you spell that for us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: D-r-a-g-a-s-o-v-a-c.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And your fellow soldiers from your unit, what about them after you left?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I asked my boss or, rather, my driver --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please speak more slowly. And could you resume from where you said: "I asked my boss or, rather, my driver," and what did you then say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
