utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to buy a souvenir or take something as a souvenir. He laughed. He said go and find something, and then I found a polystyrene sign of the 28th Division. I took it and then I proceeded where Commander Pelemis had ordered me to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not an answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What happened to the soldiers in your unit after you left?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: They stayed put, on stand by.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Until when did they stay there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. They arrived at the base on that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when it comes to your unit, how did they move to your base in Dragasovac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I arrived there first. I took one road and they arrived from two directions, one group from Zeleni Jadar, the other across Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is very important. Therefore, we -- I would suggest that we take a break first because it's already time and then continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll do that. At the same time, Mr. Lukic, it's not appropriate to tell the witness that it's important what is coming. First of all, we assume that everything you're asking the witness is important. And otherwise you shouldn't ask him. And second, it can be understood as a signal of something and that's -- rather refrain from such comments. We'll first take a break. We'll first ask that the witness to be escorted out of the courtroom. We'll take a break of 20 minutes and we'd like to see you back after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: After the break for urgent personal reasons, Judge Fluegge is unable to continue to hear this case. Judge Moloto and myself have decided that it would be in the interests of justice to continue hearing the case, and it is of short duration that Judge Fluegge will be absent. We expect him to be back tomorrow morning. We take a break and will resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you're ready, you may continue. Witness, just to explain to you, you'll see own two Judges in front of you. That is because the third Judge is for urgent personal reasons absent, and we decided that we would continue to hear the case for this short duration under Rule 15 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. So that explains why we're just the two of us here. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I continue, Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So how did the members of your unit travel? How did they arrive after you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: They travelled well, and there were no problems until the moment they left Vlasenica and arrived in front of Radosat [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What happened there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: They were in an APC and that APC overturned by a bridge and ended up 40 metres deep down in an abyss.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As the APC was turning over, did somebody get injured or hurt?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: While the AP was turning over, a man got killed. His name was Dragan Kolje [phoen]. He was a member of the sabotage unit. Another man was seriously injured. His name was --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if we could -- a little slower on the names. These are -- we didn't get the name correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could we first -- could you please repeat the name of the person that got killed. You said his name is Dragan and then could you repeat his family name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First I first have to correct you. He was not killed. He was a victim of the accident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dragan Koljivrat [Realtime transcript read in error "Koljivat"] was the name of the man who was a member of the sabotage unit who died in the accident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't suggest that anything else happened to him that than that he died in the accident. Could you also give us the second name again. The person injured. His name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His name was Mladjo. I don't know his family name. He was injured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, the family name was again misrecorded on page 48, line 8. The witness said Koljivrat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Witness, is that how you spell the name of the person who died in the accident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Koljivrat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then another person who was injured. He was the driver of the APC. That person --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, is that someone different from Mladjo, or is it ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A third person, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could you give his name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The name of the third person who was injured and who was the driver of the APC was Milorad Pelemis. He was the commander of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please -- please proceed. Next question please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you do, is the name of Mladjo, is he -- can you point it out on this list of the sabotage detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that his family name was Filipovic and that he can be found under number 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Filipovic. But that doesn't sound like Mladjo. It looks like 13 Mladenko.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, his nickname was Mladjo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since we're looking at this list anyhow, were you familiar with those who were with you on this expedition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Had you known them for a longer period of time being together in the unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was with them in the unit. And when we were supposed to get together when they recruited us from Bijeljina and Vlasenica, they were members of the Bijeljina group or the Bijeljina detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but does that mean that you had known them for how long, these other members of the group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the moment they joined us. That's when I met them all. Because I gave them uniforms, I fed them, I provided them with sports kits and everything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that for all of them at the same time or was it at different times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at different times. They did not all arrive on the same day. They did not join the unit all on the same day. However, having said that, they started serving in the unit on the same day, all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what day was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they arrived in the unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For example, for Mr. Kalajdzic, found under number 8, when would that have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They arrived in Bijeljina in 1994, when the detachment was set up. I don't recall the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we have the document on the screen, D320, the names from 1 through 15, were these people billeted in Bijeljina or in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is reading names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I looking at the right list?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Nemanja Bogart was a member of the Vlasenica detachment, so he was a signalsman. That's the order that's normally followed, officer and then the signalsman. Djoko Vukovic was a driver Vlasenica, and Milovan Milesic was a member of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'll stop you there. You're not invited to describe these persons but the question is whether, the numbers 1 through 15, whether these people were billeted in Bijeljina or in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just getting there. I wanted to tell who was in Bijeljina, who was there. I just wanted to give you that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that part of them were billeted in Bijeljina and another part was billeted in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I leave it to Mr. Lukic whether he wants this to be specified or whether we leave it to that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then the names from 16 through 24, were they mixed or did they all hail from one place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Please bear with me. From number 16, Luka Jokic, to number 24, Zoran Stupar, they are members of the Vlasenica detachment or platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just another clarification. On page 45, line 6 of today's transcript, LiveNote, you mentioned a name where your platoon's base was. Now I really have a problem. Is it Dragasovac or Dragasevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Dragasevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Koljivrat, your comrade-in-arms who lost his life, who organised the funeral?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly how it was that you organised that and who went with you, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The late Koljivrat was transferred to the Vlasenica medical centre, just like the wounded Mladjo and the wounded Pelemis. This was done by the soldiers who were there on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did you transfer him to the Vlasenica medical centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, that has to be done whenever there's a death, a wounding. A report has to be written up, why the man lost his life, so that some day somebody would be held responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you get any documentation in relation to Koljivrat's death?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he buried there in Vlasenica or was he transported further?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. Since he hailed from Trebinje, he was buried at the Koljivrat family graveyard in Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who attended the funeral with you, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The journey to Trebinje, I chose a few soldiers who went along with me: Zeljko Vukovic, Nebojsa Gagic, Srdjan Brezo, Drazan Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I think there was another soldier. There are one or two more, but I can't remember the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On which date did the funeral take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, when I took him from hospital, that was the 13th. I documented that with a certificate that I signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We still do not know yet when the funeral took place. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The funeral took place on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Until when did you stay in Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We stayed in Trebinje after the funeral on the 14th, in the afternoon. We stayed at his family, the Koljivrats.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you go back and if so when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Later. We stayed on for a while because that's some custom of theirs. We were supposed to drink some wine that the father had prepared for his son's wedding. Since he buried him on that day, then there was no point in keeping the wine so he wanted to open that wine and to thank us for having brought his son there and for the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Approximately when did you leave Trebinje to Dragasevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the evening. I don't know what time it was. It was later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So when did you arrive in the base in Dragasevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Along the way, we stopped in Pale. That's where one of the soldiers who was there with us, Srdjan Brezo, was from. So that he could see them, because they had fled from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you arrive in Dragasevac, the base there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Between 10.00 and 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you do when you arrived in base? You, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't need them for anything anymore, so I said at ease, and then I went to the office to see whether the commander was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when you say "commander," which commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you find him in the office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see him on base that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. Had I seen him, I would have given some of the gifts that the Koljivrat family had sent him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that, after that day, the 15th, when was it that you first saw Pelemis; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think somewhere around the 21st, the 22nd. I'm not sure about the dates now. It's been a very long time. It's been 20 years now. I cannot go on this way. I can just give approximate dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 21st, the 22nd. Which month, which year?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The month of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what happened after that in the base in Dragasevac? Who arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, some of the soldiers were free. Mr. Pelemis said who would be free, who would be off, and who would be on duty, who would be prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anybody arrive? Somebody who was not a member of your detachment --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't understand the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was it that arrived? I'm sorry, the interpreters did not hear your answer when I asked you about somebody who was not a member of your detachment.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pecanac came.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did Pecanac come there? What was he there for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He didn't address me personally. He addressed a soldier by the name of Zoran.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did they speak? Did you hear the conversation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: While I was there, I was jotting something down. I was copying something from a notebook that they were distributing while I was not there. And first the conversation was normal, and then there was tension on the rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, a part of this answer is pretty unclear to me. Copying something from a notebook. What notebook? That they were distributing. Who's "they"? Distributing among who? That all needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, you heard that. You heard what Judge Orie is interested in. So --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I was absent and there was a soldier there who took care of the troops, breakfast, lunch, dinner, fuel, guards, activities in the compound. He kept that internally, and I had to register that in the unit log-book, in the registry so that I could finally complete the procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What now was there that was distributed? Because you said: "I was copying something from a notebook that they were distributing." Who's "they"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The soldier, Milesic Milovan, who was standing in for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's "he" and not "they," if I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was this group of soldiers there that had to eat, sleep. Somebody had to feed them. If ten tins are issued, then that has to be written down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So distribution then refers to food and similar things to be distributed among the soldiers. Is that how I have to understand it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When this discussion was over between Zoran and -- actually, please, the record does not reflect this. You did mention the last name of this person, so in line 16, page 55 of LiveNote, the name of Zoran is referred to.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When that conversation was over between Zoran Obrenovic and Pecanac, did you talk to Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I talked to Obrenovic afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did Obrenovic say to you? What was the subject of their conversation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That he needed a group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What else did he say? Did he tell you what he needed a group of soldiers for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: For some task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we just make it clear who the "he "is that we're speaking of?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 9, I said -- I mean, it's on this page: "What did Obrenovic say to you?" And then after that, I said "he." So could you please tell us what did Obrenovic say to you? What was the subject of the conversation between him and Pecanac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Soldier Obrenovic told me verbatim that Mr. Pecanac - and he said, "this guy" - is asking me for some men so that they could go somewhere on some task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Obrenovic tell you then what kind of task?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This conversation between Obrenovic and Pecanac, was it one conducted in a friendly atmosphere or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, no. Both of them are a bit brazen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So was it a peaceful conversation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: At first it looked like a normal conversation and afterwards, tensions went up. This guy was yelling, "You have to," and this other one was yelling, "I won't. You know who it is that is issuing orders here in this compound. You go to Pelemis. If he allows it, I will carry out the task, and if he doesn't allow it, I will not do it. You can shoot me," but that's, anyway, how it went on, and that's how it ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This conversation of theirs, was it attended by Pelemis?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. Because Pecanac would not have anything to say that -- in that case, or Zoran either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the main argument of Zoran Obrenovic? Why did he not want to obey Pecanac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, he's not the commander of the sabotage detachment. It's not Pecanac. It is Milorad Pelemis, and he's the one who makes decisions about everything. And he issues orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So did some people from your detachment from Dragasevac leave after that quarrel with Pecanac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were they issued any equipment and did they take it with them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who issued the equipment to them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the vehicle they took?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The van that I took to Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who packed the equipment and put it into the van?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you pack into the van?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: PKT, 8 millimetres -- 84 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What else did you put into the van?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Ammunition for PKT.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you pack anything else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: M64 called Zolja; hand-held launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Anything else? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: A small mortar, 60 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you pack any explosives?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I did. These so-called claymore mines. MRUDs, that's also mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many MRUDs you packed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, I'll remember. I think six. Around six.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anybody examine this equipment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I packed food for 48 hours in the field, the so-called SDO. Bags; sleeping bags, that is. Also some water.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That would be it. If I've forgotten something, I just cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anybody check that equipment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Of course. Second Lieutenant Franc Kos examined it, and I asked him whether he was satisfied with it, and he said: "Is it the way it's usually done?" And he said yes, and there you go. He -- here's a sheet of paper. So that's documentation since -- and all of that was taken, and I registered all of that and it's all in the archives. And I did a proper hand-over, and all of that is there and has been there since the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I see here that mortars are being issued and mines and MRUDs. Did Kos have any objection in terms of what you had packed, this equipment, these explosives?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. He always wanted to make sure that he had everything, and he wanted land-mines. And that's good because when a unit is somewhere and then there is protection 50 or 100 metres away, then if somebody were to step on this land-mine, then the unit would realise that there was somebody coming. And that's what everybody does in the field. If people want to survive, then they have to take care. Everybody does that, let alone saboteurs like the members of our unit. It would really be a disgrace if somebody were to catch them by surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was your impression at that moment? Did Kos know what the goal of the mission was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, he did not know at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to you, who was the leader of the group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The person with the highest rank. That was Franc Kos, the most experienced saboteur and the person with the highest rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Drazan Erdemovic left with that group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't have to. However, he said everybody was there. He had to serve for three more days. He volunteered to join the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about you? Did you know what the group's task was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know then. I didn't learn even much later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to you, the rest of the men in the group who left your base, did they know what the goal of the mission was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to your best knowledge, what were they told?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask anybody nor did I have the right to inquire. I know that they left, they took the road towards Sekovici. Those lines were all controlled by our military. All the way up to Zvornik. Srebrenica had fallen, so I believe that they were sent to set up an ambush or on a reconnoitring mission to reinforce a group, or perhaps one of the officers were in the field and they -- and they needed to provide security because they didn't have anybody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, why do you believe that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because they took the weapons and equipment that are usually taken on a field mission. There was no indication that their task would be behind the lines. They didn't take any explosives, they did not ask for any special equipment that [indiscernible] could use only on repeater that we as a unit had with protected lines and encryption devices. I thought that perhaps they would be providing security for a road or perhaps they would spend a night somewhere in the field. I had just arrived. I didn't have a clue what was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it was pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't say that it was speculation. It was about sending a group on a mission. Such a group had to be provided with everything, food, water, materiel, equipment, everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah, but that doesn't explain what the purpose of that mission would be. Because whatever the mission is, you need food anyhow, you need water anyhow, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. Materiel and equipment have -- had to be given to every group on a mission. When a group works behind the lines, then different materiel and equipment are given to them, explosive, Motorolas, a different repeater. It was to be assumed that they were not going to be -- or, rather, that they were not being sent into the depth of the enemy positions but that rather they would stay close to our military positions and lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic. And may I -- you're coming close to your one and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think have some time left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Limited. I asked I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is it, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, when I asked Mr. Registrar a while ago, he said 15 minutes left and that was approximately 10 minutes ago, so that would mean, if I'm generous, six, seven minutes; otherwise just five.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm closing to an end, so I hope I will be in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I expect you to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Todorovic, that group left. And what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I stayed with another group of people, and we set out for Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you do in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We left a lorry behind. Its battery was down so we took two mobile batteries. It was marked by our initials. Nobody touched it. Still, we inspected it. We wanted to make sure that nobody had planted anything on it and we wanted to prevent casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you transport anything on that truck?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That was returned to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you gather livestock around Srebrenica and for how long?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On that day, on the following day, I went to Srebrenica. I'm not hiding anything. I didn't take anything that was not used by the unit or in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time, were there any renegade Muslim groups consisting of their combatants anywhere around the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you make contact with them? Was there shooting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, no. But on the road to Milici, somewhere below Milici they killed a married couple. They were in hiding. They did not want to be discovered. And I think that in Kupusina, perhaps some 20 days later, four Serbian lads were killed. I don't know how they found themselves there, whether they were soldiers or not. In any case, there was an errant group that had -- were captured later. They were put on trial. I believe that they were in Zvornik, and then they were released from there I think. There were proceedings against them, but I don't know what the outcome was. In any case, they were captured, none of them were injured. I don't know what was going on there. I couldn't care less, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Mr. Todorovic, thank you. That was all we had for you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Todorovic, you'll now be cross-examined. And there's still ten minutes to go before we take another break. You'll be cross-examined by Mr. McCloskey. You find him to your right. Mr. McCloskey is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we know each other from your prior testimonies in this case -- in this Tribunal, I should say.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You testified as the Prosecution in the Todorovic case -- excuse me, in the Popovic case, the Tolimir case, and the Karadzic case, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, you've mentioned this -- this group that Pecanac was organising, that you Erdemovic went, and you say Franc Kos went as well. Who else besides Franc Kos and Erdemovic went in this group?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the name slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name you mentioned a second ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Brano Gojkovic. Stanko Savanovic. Boris Popov. Six, seven, or eight men. I can't remember everybody. It was 20 years ago, but I'm sure of the three that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: If you have a name, jog my memory. I'll confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Marko?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Boskic, yes. And then Erdemovic joined them. Erdemovic volunteered. Nobody selected him. He volunteered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you later learn what that group had actually been doing when they came back from their mission?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you ever learn what that group had been doing on the 15th and/or 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Erdemovic was arrested or he surrendered - I don't know what happened - and then he told the truth about everything that they had done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And have you had a chance to speak to the Defence in this case before testifying today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, either here or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I came straight from Montenegro to the room. I never even took a stroll around the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to talk to Mr. Lukic or any of his associates before testifying today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Only when they first asked me whether I could come here and testify at the Tribunal on behalf of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And who was Pecanac, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue. Does this mean, Witness, that you didn't speak with any of the Defence team members after you arrived in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I just spoke to the member of the Tribunal services who took me -- brought me here from the airport and received me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Victims and Witness Section, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. These people, they waited for me at Amsterdam airport, they brought me to the hotel, and then they brought me to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While there is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While there's an intervention, Mr. McCloskey. At page 65, line 20, you asked the witness what was that with reference to what it is that the group had done. He never answered this question. He then told you that Erdemovic was arrested or surrendered and then he told the truth about everything, but your question was what was that that they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you clear up this for us, Witness? What was it that you learned that this group had done when they went on the mission that you have spoken of briefly today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When Erdemovic, a member of the 10th Sabotage Unit, surrendered answer and when he arrived here and when he provided a statement, at that moment I realised they that had done things that I was never aware of and that the other soldiers who were not group members also didn't know about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still not answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what you mean when I ask you when did you learn about what that group had done, had you learned that they had gone and killed many hundreds of people based on what Erdemovic told you -- or excuse me, what Erdemovic had said in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Erdemovic said that he had participated in the killings of Muslims, i.e., Bosniaks, from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you named this [sic] people that left on that mission just now, and is it your understanding that Erdemovic had named many if not the same people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I believe that he mentioned one group of people, the same group I did. I don't know if Erdemovic went on other missions when I was not there and whether another group had gone on any missions before Erdemovic and I spoke about that. I don't know. I did not have the right to ask any questions of those soldiers, nor would they have dared give me any answer, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you've testified that a Pecanac came by and wanted Zoran Obrenovic to get a group to go on this -- go on a mission. Who is Pecanac, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Pecanac was an officer. He was a member of the Main Staff and sometimes he would introduce himself as the chief of security. On other days he would introduce him as aide-de-camp. It depended on the day. I didn't socialise with him. I don't know much about them [as interpreted]. He was an officer, I was a soldier. I was a member of another unit that had its commander, that respected its commander and obeyed him without any questions asked. And Pecanac, as far as I'm concerned, I could just give him a glass of water if he got thirsty. That was it. That's the long and the short of the whole story.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You've testified before about his connection with General Mladic. Tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He -- I saw and I heard that he was a member of security. I don't know whether the general and him spoke, what they spoke about. And as far as I'm personally concerned in my unit, he didn't have anything to do with us. And whatever happened was of his own accord. Nobody issued any orders. The general didn't and Pelemis didn't. Somebody should inform at least the command in Bijeljina where there was a desk officer on duty. Somebody should have picked up a phone and should have asked somebody if --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, this is very simple question and answer. You've described him as General Mladic's aide-de-camp or adjunct haven't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's he introduced himself to me. So I stick by that. Sometimes he would say that he was the chief of security. I don't know what he was. I don't even know what the term "adjutant" means, whether it's a rank or something else. I just remember the term that he used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when you say chief of security, do you mean personal-type of security or are you talking chief of security a la security officers for the Drina Corps or the Main Staff or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He could not be in the Drina Corps. He was affiliated with the Main Staff. I don't know whether he [indiscernible] for the personnel, the barracks, or the general personally. Obviously, each general in the army had his security. I don't know who it was in this case. That's how he introduced himself to me. I didn't ask for any IDs. I just take that at its face value.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think it's break time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is, Mr. McCloskey. Before we take that break, I've got one question for you, Witness, which is the following. Pelemis who was in command was absent. You said: I saw him only back after the 21st or 22nd of July. Who replaced him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, it should have been either the Slovenian or Luka Jokic. Our territory was in Vlasenica, so it should have been Luka Jokic. But he wasn't there. I don't know where he was. Maybe he was in the corps or perhaps at home. Maybe he had gone home to change his clothes or something. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who do you say you don't know where he was? You mean Pelemis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about Jokic. Pelemis had been injured before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now if Pelemis is supposed to be replaced by Jokic, who would be replacing Jokic, if Jokic wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If something had to be done within the barracks perimeter, for example, receiving an order or mail, it would have been me, if I was there. And as for the rest, it had to be left with the person at sentry duty who would then inform Commander Pelemis either by phone or by the corps mail. I don't know how but I know that one could send that information by phone or by a different communications device. It really didn't matter much that he was at hospital. He could have still been informed and kept abreast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you followed the conversation between Pecanac and Obrenovic, if I understood you well. You described that conversation. What was your position --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not Pelemis, Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think I said Obrenovic but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Pecanac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now what do you think about what they discussed? Should a group be assembled and be sent on a mission, or should you, you were -- at that moment, you said you should replace Jokic. Were you considering that it should not -- that what Pecanac had requested should not be done or that it should be done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If he had asked me, I would not have allowed him to do that. I would have sent him packing and I would have asked him to bring back a document. I would have reacted differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, who ordered you to prepare all the ammunition that you packed? Who did order you to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the vehicle pulled over in front of the garage, the Slovenian got out. And when he said combat kit, I knew. I knew exactly what I should do just like every other time because I was in control of everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who was the Slovenian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that he was either a lieutenant. He was a member of the sabotage unit, just like me. He was Slovenian by origin. I don't know how come he was a member of our unit and I never researched that. He was a member of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he order you to pack all this ammunition and have it loaded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He told me prepare everything that we need for a mission, and I set out to carry out the order immediately. And he signed the request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And he was superior to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment he was, indeed. Because all I went by were the ranks of my officers. I was not at all interested in the ranks of others. Pecanac certainly could not have issued me any orders because he was not a member of my unit. He did not have the right to give me orders. He did not have authority over my unit, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you accepted an order from the Slovenian of which you said a minute ago: "... he was either a lieutenant. A member of the sabotage unit, just like me." You accepted his orders. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I gave it a bit of a thought. I wanted to avoid any conflicts. I thought, ah, well, I should comply with requests of both sides. I first wanted them to talk to Pelemis, but everything was done in a haste, so I said, well, come as it may and to hell with it. If I'd personally been asked and consulted, I would never have allowed that to happen. If the mail had arrived in my hands, if it contained an order, I would have acted differently. I would have called everything off for at least half an hour pending a final solution, because things were done without any papers, orders. It wasn't preceded by any telephone conversation. The guy came into the barracks, he wanted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, a minute ago you told us that if Pelemis was not there it was Jokic who would replace him. Then I asked you who would be in charge if Jokic wasn't there, and you said it was you yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pecanac never ever spoke to me about any tasks or missions. I did not interfere. I would have interfered if I had gotten an order from the Main Staff sent to Pelemis, from Pelemis to me, and then whatever was contained in that order, I should have obeyed that and I would have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the very end, you assisted in providing the ammunition and whatever was needed for that mission.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and we'll resume at quarter to 2.00. But you first follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, The Slovene, that was the nickname for Franc Kos; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And tell us the first name of Pecanac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I think his name was Dragomir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was his rank back in July 1995, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: A captain or a major. One of the two. Major, rather. Maybe ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And you've acknowledged you testified at the Popovic case, and I'm going to take us there and ask you a question or two about Pecanac's position, something that you told us back then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 32552. Should be page 25 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this will just be English, so I'll read it slowly. And on line 6, you say: "After a while, Mr. Pecanac arrived." And you're asked: "That's not a name we've heard before. Can you tell us who Mr. Pecanac is, a name during your testimony, you didn't mention him before, who he is?" And your answer was: "He was the head of security, general's aide-de-camp. I don't know how I should put it. He was always with him. He carried out his orders and looked after his security and he had some troops who provided security with him." And this reference to "him" and "he," that's General Mladic, I take it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's how he introduced himself to us when we saw him in the field and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And my question is: But your reference to "he" in this question was you were referring to that Pecanac was General Mladic's aide?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's how he introduced himself to us and I accept that. I mean, that's what he said and that's what I'm saying to you and that's what I said to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You also say in this answer: "He was always with him," meaning General Mladic was always with him. So ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, General Mladic cannot be with him. He was supposed to be near General Mladic. All the officers of our army liked to be close to General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. But in this sentence, you tell the Court that Pecanac was always with General Mladic; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Nearby, by him, around him. Now, whatever all that means. He said that he was there. Maybe he was just carrying papers around. I wasn't there by Pecanac and the general.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You also say that Pecanac carried out Mladic's orders. So as far as you knew, Pecanac would carry out General Mladic's orders; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Of course. He wouldn't be carrying out my orders. I carried out the orders of my commander too, whatever it was that he ordered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you have in your various statements and testimonies mentioned another senior officer that came by the -- Dragasevac on the 15th that day, with Pecanac, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Did Popovic come by with Pecanac that day on the 15th to Dragasevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Judging by the car and the licence plates, it's a car of the Drina Corps. He drove it, or his driver, and I claim with full responsibility to this day that Popovic did not enter the compound. His vehicle was outside the compound, say, about 30 metres away. But I know that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did -- you've always said that a -- a gate officer reported who was in that vehicle to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The officer from the gate said that Mr. Popovic's vehicle -- well, maybe that was a mistake in interpretation or translation. But I never said that he reported to Mr. Popovic personally. He only could have greeted Mr. Pecanac when entering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, whatever you testified in this Court can you verified on the basis of the audio recordings, and then the interpretation can be verified as well. Is it your position that you never said that he reported to Mr. Popovic personally? Is that your position? Because then we'll verify it. If you insist --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who's "he"? I don't insist. But I just want to know who "he" is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I leave this in your hands because I do not know whether he reported to Mr. Popovic, whether that is exactly what was said or not. I just wanted to intervene to tell the witness that whatever he thinks is caused by an ill-interpretation, that we can verify it. I leave it in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Witness, let's see if can I help you. We're going to go to the next page of your Popovic testimony back in 2007, and you may remember I asked you this question on line 18: "All right. And did you actually see Mr. Popovic outside the gate with his car or did someone just tell you that he was there?"

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This should be page 27.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. That was my question. And your answer: "The gate-keeper told us that Officer Popovic was outside. This person who was working, providing security for the base. I suppose that he must have seen his car and he must have assumed that he was there. I'm sure he knew him." And then if we go to page 40 in e-court, Judge Kwon asked you on line 11: "Mr. Todorovic, you told us that you heard from the gate-keeper that Mr. Popovic was outside; is that correct? "THE WITNESS: [Interpretation] Yes."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, misinterpretation. It cannot be an officer at the gate. It can be a gate-keeper. It is the gate-keeper that told me that Popovic's vehicle was parked about 20 metres away from the gate. We did not have an officer at the gate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the issue is not whether it was an officer but whether the person at the gate, the gate-keeper, that you heard from that person that Mr. Popovic was outside, which you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I heard that from him, and then I paid attention to the vehicle and I saw the vehicle. It was a cherry-coloured Golf of the Drina Corps, Drina Corps licence plates. He did not get out of the car, but I know the vehicle of the Drina Corps that Mr. Popovic drove, said that it was his vehicle. It should have been him or his driver or someone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you were told that it was Mr. Popovic and you saw a car which supported --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I did not walk up. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And getting back to your account when Pecanac told Zoran Obrenovic to get a group of people together, and you say Zoran Obrenovic refused. And then you've told us before that Pecanac focused his energies on another soldier and issued him the same directive. Can you tell us who that was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Brano Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did Pecanac said to Brano Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I guess the same thing he said to Zoran.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't want you to guess. What did he say? You were there. We don't need exact words.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, issued him the same order that he had issued to Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I'm -- Brano Gojkovic knew who Pecanac was as you did, did he not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, you've also told us that you've heard Pecanac talking about another senior officer. Did Pecanac -- did you hear Pecanac say anything about Beara?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That he should see him, meet up with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So explain that, more detail.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, if he were to go with that group, then he should meet with Officer Beara on the Sekovici -- no, Dragasevac-Sekovici-Zvornik road. No. Either, in Sekovici or in Zvornik. I don't know exactly. I wasn't present. I don't know where they met. Maybe it was Zvornik or Sekovici where they met up. I didn't ask Pecanac where he met up with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So Pecanac was ordering Gojkovic to take this group and meet up with Beara.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you've also talked about being a logistics officer and providing ammunition and some other materiels. Do you remember providing an actual handwritten document of some materiel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 05676.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: This is a document that was written by soldier Milesic, Milovan. This is an internal paper that he got --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness repeat his answer. It was not understood.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We have already said the witness is unintelligible. Could he please repeat his answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, knowing that you're on the English channel I thought that you would take action. I left it to you. Witness, could you restart your answer. Perhaps, Mr. McCloskey, if you would repeat the question, that would certainly assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could I just ask you what this was.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: This was an internal paper that was used by soldier Milesic, Milovan on the 14th when I was not there, and he wrote down what it was that he issued to some people. As for this ammunition, I don't know who he gave it to. I just registered it in my archives. And then down it says fish, pate, spam, paprika as usual. Now, was this issued to the kitchen? And then this first thing. Was it issued to some soldier as welfare?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Slow down. We're having a hard time translating you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this is a document that you have provided, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this is material that went to the group with Brano Gojkovic on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, I issued everything on the 15th of July, whatever was needed. Fish, cold cuts. This is not something that should be sent with anybody on a field mission. Milovan Milesic, this is his handwriting. This is an internal document. This is to cover the things that were issued from the storage. I copied that into my records. At the end of war, I handed over all of my records. I this is not my handwriting. I can prove that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The paper, actually, is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we see special police detachment Sekovici on the top. Was that the unit that you were part of for a while and you weren't happy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so this notepad that this was written on was yours, as you just said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It is possible that I brought it over from the unit. Well, I'm sure that I did, and I gave it to him to write on it. This is an internal document. I don't know if you know the meaning of the word "internal." I used this paper to make official records, and then when my duty is over, I hand the records over to in my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And looking at the 16 July entries, I'm interested in the ammunition for M-84, 1200 pieces. Is that the big machine-gun you spoke about giving the group of Brano Gojkovic in your direct testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: This is ammo for M-84, which is a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's the same -- for the same kind of machine-gun that you gave to the Brano Gojkovic group that you spoke about in direct testimony; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I gave one to The Slovenian on the 15th. This is not my handwriting. It is my notepad, it belongs to my unit, but not my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'd offer this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7379, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go very briefly back to 1992. You said you were in the Birac Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can we have 65 ter 32578.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who was the commander of your brigade, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He was a captain by rank or perhaps it was even higher. Svetozar Andric was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Take a look at this, what's identified as a document from 10 July 1992 as an early promotion for Svetozar Andric, son of Petko. Was that your commander that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you recall him getting a promotion while you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would offer this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7380, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who was your battalion commander while you were at the Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I was in our Pelemis unit up to the 1st of September. That's where I was assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In the village of Pelemisi?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Milorad Pelemis has told us that during the summer of 1992 they held some women captive there at Pelemisi. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were not held captive. They were brought in order to be exchanged for some people in Kladanj. Stanimir, who was the police commander, tried to do that because one of the policemen from his unit who was also -- actually, he was an inspector, had been taken prisoner over there, so he wanted to use those women and exchange them for that prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So were they there voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how they came. I didn't ask too many questions. I had a different job. I guarded the line. That was not my responsibility. That was not my call. I did not attend the negotiations between him and the other gentleman whose family name was also Pelemis. His first name was Stanimir and he was the police commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31647.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it. Witness, you say, well, you are asking too many questions to you. But you said they were not held captive, so you claim to have some knowledge about whether they were there voluntarily on whether they were not free to move?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in one part of the village. I would go to the command from time to time. Everybody moved around. There was no school there. There was no prison there. There were no bars on any windows. All the houses were just normal village houses. Not too big.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you see those women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By the water well, in the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You told us that they were there to be exchanged. Is it your view that if you are held ready for exchange that you are free to just go your own way or is it ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We tried to establish communications with the -- the other municipality of Kladanj using an R -- RUP-station. I don't know how they did that, why they did that. I was not part of that. But I know that they were there. They were doing laundry by the well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not an answer to my question, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And were they fraternising with your young Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean "fraternising"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were they enjoying their company? Were the women enjoying the company of your Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't understand the word "enjoy." What do you mean, did they have cups of coffee, did they share food with them? What do you mean by that? I mean, the -- maybe socialising, what we call socialising in Bosnia is sitting down over a cup of coffee and joking and talking, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, were the women socialising with the Serb soldiers, one or more?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: There were some older geezers that guarded them. They had coffees with them. Momir Gazevic [phoen], he was one of the locals. Well, his name was also Pelemis. And there was another, Sadaj [phoen], I don't know what his name was, Ratko, it was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at this document. This is just my final question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Those houses were on the front line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Those -- they were guarded, if I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just looking at this -- I'd like to ask you about this Slobodan Pajic, son of Milos. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Where from? There were a lot of Pajics there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You can see that he was a battalion commander for your brigade, the Birac Brigade in August of 1992. Not saying he had to do anything with Pelemisi. I just want to know if you remember him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I see in the English translation that a person by the name of Slobodan Pajic -- oh, yes. I see it on the right-hand side it's slightly different from what we see on the left-hand side. But it's a proposal for appointment of commanding officers. Then I think the appropriate question to be put to the witness would be whether he is aware that a Slobodan Pajic who was described as a clerical officer for logistic operations and deputy commander for logistics was proposed for being appointed as, well, as infantry battalion commander. But, again, it's -- the text of the document is not entirely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, that's one reason why I was asking him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We see here, sir, that it says "currently Vlasenica infantry battalion commander," and we see the date of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that the date of it or is that the date of birth?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, just the date up -- 23 August 1992 is the date of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So just in looking at this, does this look like a document from your brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It says that this is from the Vlasenica Battalion and the battalion of the Birac Brigade was in Trnovo, if that's the same Slobodan Pajic, son of Milos.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about Rade Bogunovic? You'd certainly have heard it from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know that my colleague McCloskey is passionate about his work, but our working day is over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, your working day is not over yet, but court time is over, Mr. Lukic, that's not the same. Mr. McCloskey, indeed, my fellow Judge Moloto also hinted that I'd forgotten about the time. So did you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would offer this into evidence. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing further in cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If I can get this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P738 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only if it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Could you please, Mr. Registrar, could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 31647 is Exhibit P7381, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before you admit, I would object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is -- yes, you would like to object.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. First, this witness has no knowledge about this and there is no stamp, there is no any kind of verification of this document. At least what we have. I have only one page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, any answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I was going through the document to check his familiarity. We can do it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would have you further questions for the witness anyhow Mr. -- I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you switch on your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 10, 15 minutes probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that the witness cannot be excused yet. Therefore, Mr. McCloskey, if you would pay attention to this tomorrow to start with, and then have you an opportunity to re-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I -- just out of the realistic thought that perhaps I may think of a few more questions overnight, if you could leave me with a little bit of flexibility. I won't be long and I hope not to have any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I do not intervene in -- when our working days end, I also do not intervene in what you do at night as far as thinking of further questions. We'll see tomorrow what will come up and you'll have an opportunity at least to put a limited number of questions tomorrow morning. Mr. Todorovic, we'd like to see you back tomorrow, but I first instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony given today or whether that is testimony still to be given tomorrow. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise to all those who suffered from me not I'm looking at the clock consistently, and luckily enough both Mr. Lukic and my fellow Judge Moloto did a better job in that respect. We adjourn for the day and will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 12th of May, 2015, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 12th day of May, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.24 p.m.,
